research_questions: Does each trained shared policy outperform its exact untrained initialization on unseen procedural seeds and environments?
Does validation improvement transfer to the held-out distribution?
How large is the validation-to-test generalization gap?
How do trained policies compare with random and frontier baselines?
Which positive and negative conclusions are supported by the evidence?

evaluation.episode_order: policy order below; within each policy reference environment then structural environment; seeds ascending

reference_environment.role: unseen procedural seeds in the training structure

metrics.raw_reward_role: within-environment diagnostic only; never the primary metric and never used for incompatible cross-environment or cross-reward conclusions

diagnostic_definitions.targets_observed: Count of distinct true target cells that entered at least one agent's configured local observation radius; centralized target state is used only by the evaluator metric, never by a policy.
diagnostic_definitions.discovery_to_recovery_conversion: targets_recovered divided by targets_observed, defined as zero when targets_observed is zero.
diagnostic_definitions.blocked_movements: Count of non-STAY movement attempts reported blocked by the simulator.
diagnostic_definitions.collisions: Count of non-STAY movement attempts blocked by another agent through a contested destination, swap, movement cycle, or occupied-agent dependency; wall, boundary, and obstacle blocks are excluded.

aggregation.episode_level: For each policy and environment, retain all 100 ordered episode rows and report mean, sample standard deviation, minimum, maximum, and the configured deterministic 95% percentile bootstrap interval with 2000 resamples.
aggregation.held_out_policy_value: Equal-episode pooled mean over the 100 reference-structure test episodes and 100 structural test episodes.
aggregation.training_seed_level: For trained and exact-untrained policies, report every seed separately and aggregate the three seed-level held-out values using mean, sample standard deviation, minimum, maximum, and a deterministic 95% percentile bootstrap interval with 10000 resamples. This interval is descriptive and is not a significance test.
aggregation.pairing: Trained-minus-untrained is paired by training seed, environment, and ordered episode seed. Trained-minus-random and trained-minus-frontier use the same environment and ordered episode seed. No failed or zero-success seed may be omitted.
aggregation.baseline_reuse: Random and frontier are executed once per environment; their aligned episode rows are paired with each learned policy without rerunning the baseline.

generalization_gaps.positive_interpretation: A positive gap means held-out degradation relative to validation.
generalization_gaps.validation_sources: runs/day6/seed-{0,1,2}/best-comparison aligned validation artifacts; random and frontier are the stored identical validation baselines

classification_rule_order: evaluation_failure: any missing policy/seed/environment, non-finite value, alignment defect, preregistration mismatch, checkpoint mutation, or unusable technical result prevents a valid conclusion

reproducible_task_learning_and_transfer: every trained seed has positive paired success improvement over exact untrained, aggregate trained success exceeds random, and trained targets recovered and completion progress also exceed both exact untrained and random

negative_transfer: trained success is lower than exact untrained, or when success ties, mean trained completion progress is lower with at least two of three seed-paired differences non-positive and at least one strictly negative

exploration_transfer_without_task_completion: all trained held-out success rates are zero, negative-transfer conditions are false, and at least two of three trained seeds have positive paired coverage or targets-recovered improvement
weak_or_inconsistent_transfer: at least one trained seed improves success, targets recovered, or completion progress over exact untrained, but the reproducible-transfer rule is not met
no_meaningful_transfer: none of the preceding evidence categories applies

integrity_protocol.checkpoint_preflight: Verify checkpoint file, actor, critic, optimizer-state, candidate, reward, environment, training-seed, and selected-step identities before creating the consumption record.
integrity_protocol.immutability: Fingerprint checkpoint files and loaded actor, critic, and optimizer states before and after evaluation; all must match.
integrity_protocol.rng: Neural policies use deterministic masked argmax and consume no policy RNG. Random and frontier use explicit per-episode, per-agent derived seeds. Torch process RNG state must match before and after each neural suite.
integrity_protocol.learning: Never construct or step an optimizer; never update actor, critic, checkpoint, or training state.
integrity_protocol.one_time: Atomically claim configs/evaluation/final_test_consumed.json after all non-test preflight checks and immediately before the first test episode; any existing claim blocks evaluation.
integrity_protocol.protocol_lock: The byte-level SHA-256 of this authoritative JSON preregistration is passed to the final command and recorded in every final artifact. The scientific protocol must not be edited after the first episode begins.
integrity_protocol.failures: A preflight failure consumes no seed. A failure after the atomic claim remains visible and blocks an ordinary rerun; any later authorized replication must use a new untouched partition.

success_interpretation: Support requires held-out task-metric improvement under the ordered classification rules; exploration alone is not task completion.
failure_interpretation: Zero success, inconsistent seed effects, baseline inferiority, negative transfer, or integrity failure must remain explicit and must not be reframed as successful AI.
post_test_rules: no Day 9 work before report completion
